scope: Corollary 1.3 (Singular ranks and full-deck mixing) of the manuscript “Compatibility entropy and the spectrum of a Thorp sweep” (preprints/Compatibility-entropy-and-the-spectrum-of-a-Thorp-sweep-September-26-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 238 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 dae8f5ca5b99fbec), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF pages 4-5. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. The quote crosses a page break and includes whatever the extraction places there, such as a page number. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: For every nontrivial λ ⊢ n and 1 ≤ r ≤ Dλ, sr(Tn,λ) ≤ (16Dλr)−1/(2p∗) . If sj(Tn) denotes the full regular singular list, including all multiplicities and zeros, then sj(Tn) ≤ j−1/(2p∗) (1 ≤ j ≤ n!). 4 The constant singular value is the first value. The physical Thorp chain has worst-start 1/4 mixing time Θ(d); more precisely its lower bound is 2d−O(1). For every fixed integer M > p∗, the worst-start total-variation distance after Md physical shuffles tends to zero as d → ∞.
